analysis.title: GS Sousa - STS Insights | Systematic Dispersion: The Vol Trade of 2026
key_insights: Dispersion has been one of the most talked-about trades of 2026. The gap between single-stock and index implied volatility, driven by the AI narrative and sector/factor rotation, powered returns all year.

Implied correlation sat near historical lows and realized correlation fell further, so Dispersion strategies delivered strong risk-adjusted returns. Single-stock earnings jumps also exceeded implied moves (AMZN +15.32% Jul 31, MSFT +15.51% Jul 30, NVDA +7.87% Feb 6), so both return sources paid off together.

GS splits realized correlation (RC) into intra-sector and inter-sector components. Inter-sector RC compressed to about 0% by late summer, its most extreme level YTD, while intra-sector RC stayed range-bound.
GS expects room for Dispersion to keep performing if sector narratives keep diverging. Between-sector correlation compression is the main marginal driver, not a broad re-rating of index correlation.

Desk view (Gasparotto): GS SPX Gamma-Weighted Enhanced Dispersion (GSVIDUG6) rose 20%+ from April to July before the early August vol meltdown gave some back. Long vol on the highest-implied names since April (MU, AMD, SNDK) worked, because high implied vol flagged where realized vol would show up.

The desk sees the post-reset setup as more attractive. The implied spread is materially lower, so a repeat of August is seen as unlikely. Catalysts still in place: earnings dispersion, AI and AI sub-pocket rotation, and LETF outstanding shares that have not come down (the AUM drop came from spot selling off).

Vehicle choice: GS SPX Vega-Weighted Downside Dispersion (GSVIDUV9) picks up SPX skew carry. GS SPX Vega-Weighted Enhanced Dispersion (GSVIDUV6) fits the spot-up/vol-up single-name regime better. The desk says a repeat of the Jan-Jul path is unlikely but that should not discourage putting on dispersion now.

Downside Dispersion (launched summer 2025) gets richer carry on the short index leg from elevated put skew and concentrates the single-stock leg on downside strikes. It gives up upside earnings convexity, so it tends to beat the flagship in bearish scenarios and bleeds more in bullish ones.

The NDX dispersion suite, offered since spring 2026, mirrors the SPX construction. GS says running SPX and NDX together adds diversification because NDX's capped weighting flattens top-of-index concentration, and only about 20 names overlap between the NDX top-30 and SPX top-50.

Thematic Dispersion pairs long vol on a thematic single-stock basket (Semiconductor, AI, Mag7) with short vol on SPX or NDX. The flagship runs at a 6-month tenor to capture single-stock vol supply from structured products.

Dynamic Dispersion lets clients submit their own underliers and weights, traded as strangles or variance-swap replications against an SPX or NDX short-vol leg. GS is also researching signal tilts away from market-cap weighting (Barra factors, RV-IV spread, skew, vol-of-vol, structured-product and levered-ETF positioning).

A flagship basket can carry 20,000+ live positions daily. GS rebuilt reporting to show aggregated Greeks and Greeks decomposition at basket, leg and underlier level, top/bottom contributors, and a spot/vol shock grid.

Standard shock analysis applies the same shock to both legs, which implies 100% correlation and overstates stress losses. GS's new method embeds an explicit correlation assumption in the stock-leg shock and reports a break-even correlation per stress cell.

For GSVIDUV6 on 25-Sep-2026, the -15% spot / +10% vol stress cell breaks even at implied correlation of about 29% when realized correlation is set at 1.5x current implied (28% vs 19% currently implied). GS calls this comfortably above current implied and consistent with the ~40% 6m realized peak during Liberation Day.

With no correlation shock (realized = implied at 19%), GSVIDUV6 shock returns range from -8% to +67% of notional, with the best cell at +15% spot / +30% vol. The mildly negative cells are small-spot / vol-down scenarios, where gamma-theta support cannot offset long-vega drag.

From a vol relative-value view, GS says dispersion has outperformed analogous long/short vol variants in recent years. The Theta-Weighted version (GSVIDUT6) is pitched as an alternative to shorting 3-month index variance, and the Gamma-Weighted version (GSVIDUG6) as an alternative to outright long single-stock vol.

trade_ideas.description: Long GS SPX Vega-Weighted Downside Dispersion (GSVIDUV9): long single-stock downside-strike vol against short SPX vol, capturing SPX skew carry
trade_ideas.rationale: It picks up SPX skew carry and outperforms the flagship in bearish scenarios.
trade_ideas.risk: Gives up upside earnings convexity, so the single-stock leg bleeds more in bullish regimes.

trade_ideas.description: Long GS SPX Vega-Weighted Enhanced Dispersion (GSVIDUV6): long single-stock vol against short SPX vol, 6-month tenor
trade_ideas.rationale: It fits the spot-up / vol-up single-name regime better.
trade_ideas.risk: Mildly negative in small-spot / vol-down scenarios, where gamma-theta support is limited and long-vega drag dominates.

trade_ideas.description: Thematic dispersion: long vol on Semiconductor, AI or Mag7 single-stock baskets against short SPX or NDX vol
trade_ideas.rationale: A relative-value trade on thematic single-stock vol versus index vol.

trade_ideas.description: GS SPX Theta-Weighted Dispersion (GSVIDUT6) as an alternative to shorting 3-month index variance, and GS SPX Gamma-Weighted Dispersion (GSVIDUG6) as an alternative to outright long single-stock vol
trade_ideas.rationale: The relative-value construction makes dispersion a more balanced exposure than outright long or short vol.

risk_factors: A repeat of the early August vol meltdown, which gave back part of the Apr-Jul gains. The desk sees this as less likely now that the implied spread is lower.
The Jan-Jul catalyst mix was unique and a repeat of that path is unlikely.
Downside Dispersion bleeds in bullish regimes because it lacks upside convexity.
In large spot moves correlations would be expected to pick up, offsetting some gains.
Small-spot / vol-down scenarios are mildly negative because gamma-theta support cannot offset long-vega drag.
Replication limits such as strike cutoffs in the index leg may skew the gamma profile and sensitivity to large shocks.
vol_and_positioning: Implied correlation sat near historical lows through 2026 and realized correlation fell further.
Inter-sector realized correlation compressed to about 0% by late summer, its most extreme level YTD. Intra-sector realized correlation stayed range-bound.
Implied correlation on GSVIDUV6 was 19% as of 25-Sep-2026.
The early August vol meltdown gave back part of the 20%+ Apr-Jul gain in GSVIDUG6. The implied spread is now materially lower.
LETF outstanding shares have not come down. The AUM drop was driven by spot selling off, so exposure could ramp back up quickly.
Highest-implied-vol names since April were MU, AMD and SNDK, and long vol on them was a very good trade.
Elevated index put skew gives richer carry on the short index leg of Downside Dispersion.
The ~40% 6m realized correlation peak during Liberation Day is the reference stress level.

tension_points.bull_case: Post-reset, the implied spread is materially lower. Earnings dispersion, AI sub-pocket rotation and still-high LETF shares remain as catalysts. Between-sector correlation compression can keep driving returns.
tension_points.bear_case: A repeat of the Jan-Jul path is unlikely given how unique that catalyst mix was. The early August vol meltdown gave back part of the Apr-Jul gains.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Correlations rising in large spot moves, which would offset gains. GS's stress cell of -15% spot / +10% vol breaks even at about 29% implied correlation with realized set at 1.5x implied.
